title: On h-Compactness, Identification Maps and Normality
content: Let \((X,\tau)\) be a topological space and \(\tau_h(X)\) denote the topology formed by the \(h\)-open subsets of \(X\). We develop compactness-transfer results for mappings, identification topologies and normality through the associated-space method. We first strengthen the compact-to-closed principle: if \(f:(X,\tau)\to(Y,\sigma)\) is \(h\)-continuous, \(X\) is \(h\)-compact and \(Y\) is a \(KC\)-space, then the continuous associated-domain map \(f:(X,\tau_h(X))\to(Y,\sigma)\) is closed. Thus a surjective such map is an ordinary identification map. At the fully associated level we introduce \(h\)-\(KC\) spaces and \(h\)-identification maps. An \(h\)-identification map is precisely a surjection whose associated-space map \((X,\tau_h(X))\to(Y,\sigma_h(Y))\) is an identification map. We establish its quotient-space and universal properties, prove an \(h\)-analogue of the classical open/closed criterion, and show that every \(h\)-irresolute surjection from an \(h\)-compact space onto an \(h\)-\(KC\) space is an \(h\)-identification map. In particular, the latter holds for \(h\)-\(T_2\) codomains. These results extend the classical identification-space arguments to the associated topology and sharpen the corresponding Hausdorff statements.We then distinguish ordinary compactness from \(h\)-compactness in connection with normality. A self-contained four-point example is both compact and \(h\)-compact but is neither normal nor \(h\)-normal. An infinite \(T_1\) example satisfying \(\tau_h(X)=\tau\) (hence \(h\)-fixed) shows that the same failure occurs when the original and associated topologies coincide. For comparison, every \(h\)-compact \(h\)-\(T_2\) space is \(h\)-normal, whereas every Hausdorff \(h\)-compact space is normal. The resulting implication diagram and compatible-product remarks locate the exact role played by the associated topology.
